requirement:
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`once` for OpenAI and `confirm` for other backends. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies. Under `once`, each subject
MUST receive a single assessment per round (including model escalation under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.adaptive`), whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.policy` has no structural obligations, and it has no implementation edges. Each clause states observable behavior. Every alternative I considered keeps the behavior and still satisfies the text.

- "Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy, `confirm` or `once`." An implementation could use an enum, a string or a strategy object and behave the same. The text names no type or interface.
- The policy source order is `--policy`, then the configuration's `policy`, then the backend default (`once` for OpenAI, `confirm` otherwise). This could be one resolver function or several inline checks. The result is the same, so how it is built is discretionary.
- "Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as `requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies." and "Under `once`, each subject MUST receive a single assessment per round." These describe assessment counts and outcomes. The confirmation requirement's own obligations are about behavior: a first `false` finishes the round, and `true` or FIXME gets exactly one independent second assessment. They are cited, not delegated as structure.
- "An unknown policy name MUST be rejected as invalid configuration or arguments." This is observable error behavior, with no prescribed mechanism.
- "The completion report MUST name the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it." This is output content. Any internal representation that produces the same report and records satisfies it.

The cited requirements `requirements.authoring.confirmation` and `requirements.authoring.adaptive` only supply context. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence here. Behavioral test coverage belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation in `requirements.authoring.policy`.

- **Precedence of the policy source.** `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[policy_comes_from_the_flag_then_the_configuration_then_defaults_to_confirm]` runs four cases:
  - no flag and no configured policy gives `confirm`;
  - `--policy once` with no configured policy gives `once`;
  - `--policy once` overrides a configured `confirm`;
  - a configured `once` is used when no flag is given.
  Each case asserts the policy named in the report, the number of model conversations, and the `policy` field of every usage record.
- **Default by backend.** `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_policy_defaults_to_once_without_changing_explicit_policy]` shows OpenAI defaults to `once`, an explicit `confirm` is kept, and the flag overrides the configured policy. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips]` shows an ollama backend defaults to `confirm`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` checks the OpenAI default end to end: usage records say `once`, and an explicit `policy = 'confirm'` gives two mini assessments.
- **`confirm` behavior.** The `--all --policy confirm` test, `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[confirm_with_all_runs_a_second_assessment_for_each_batch_subject]`, checks that every subject gets exactly two assessments, with the second marked "(second assessment)". The confirmation requirement's own selection and outcome rules are cited context and are not reassessed here.
- **`once` behavior.** The `once` cases in the policy test show one conversation per subject. The adaptive tests show a single assessment, with model escalation, recorded as the evidence. The mini-false to Sol-false case in `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[adaptive_sol_failure_is_final_and_confirm_selects_the_failed_assessment]` records `determination` false with Sol's rationale.
- **Unknown policy name.** The policy test rejects `--policy twice`, with the error naming `unknown assessment policy "twice"`. It also rejects a configured `policy = 'twice'` for both the single-requirement and `--all` forms. The error names the config file and `policy`, and no model request is made. `authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips` also rejects `'twice'`, `'Confirm'` and `true` at parse time.
- **Report names the policy.** The policy test asserts `; policy X` on stdout, `policy once` on stderr under `--stdout`, and the batch summary `...; policy once`.
- **Usage records identify the policy.** The policy test, both adaptive tests, and the `assert_policy` helper check the `policy` field of every usage record.
- **Forms covered.** The tests cover several `habeas author` forms: a single requirement, `--all`, `--stdout`, and `sites:requirements.spread --policy once`. The sites test checks that both usage records say `once`.

No gap found.

text: :::{req} policy
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`once` for OpenAI and `confirm` for other backends. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation` specifies. Under `once`, each subject
MUST receive a single assessment per round (including model escalation under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.adaptive`), whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
:::{req} confirmation
Under `confirm`, a first `false` MUST finish the round for that subject. After
`true` or FIXME, the harness MUST obtain exactly one independent second assessment
of the same subject, with the same mandatory inputs and source state. Each
assessment may discover additional inputs and has its own usage record under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.
:::{req} adaptive
Adaptive is experimental and requires explicit opt-in. For the OpenAI backend,
`model = "adaptive"` MUST select models locally rather
than send `adaptive` to the API. An assessment with an applicable existing
FIXME reference MUST go directly to `gpt-6.1-sol`. Otherwise it MUST begin with
`gpt-5.4-mini`: a true judgment is accepted, while false, FIXME, or a failed
conversation/submission MUST trigger one fresh Sol assessment. Sol's result
MUST be final for that assessment, including a false judgment or failure.
Provider errors, cancellation, mandatory-input failures, connection failures,
and usage-storage failures MUST NOT trigger model escalation.
Applicable FIXMEs MUST follow the subject's existing scope rules: requirement
references outside its own distributed sites, or the reviewed site's own FIXMEs.
Citation reviews have no applicable acknowledgments. Matching a literal word
inside unrelated text MUST NOT trigger pre-escalation.
Both tiers MUST inherit the selected credentials, endpoint, and inference
options. Explicit concrete model IDs MUST bypass adaptive routing. Each actual
model attempt MUST have a separate usage record with its real model name;
the adaptive record MUST link its attempts and record any routing reason.
Escalation MUST NOT persist intermediate mini evidence or pass mini's rationale
to Sol. Under explicit `confirm`, each independent assessment MUST use adaptive
routing. The harness MUST select the outcome under {cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation.selection`. Adaptive routing MUST NOT perform sampled audits.
